utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If I could remind you, Mr. Sikimic, of the affirmation you took at the commencement of your evidence which still applies. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Somers: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Sikimic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sikimic, do you have in front of you, please, the war diary that is marked for identification number -- Madam, if you could help me. It's 96, I believe?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask that it be placed in front of you, please. Okay. 92, I beg your pardon. I'm so sorry, it's 92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have it marked as 96.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I have just been misinformed by my own side. I apologise. 96. Yes. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you, please, to take a look on page 68 in your Serbo-Croatian version, 68, please. At 9.50, there's an entry. It says: "Jovanovic: Kovacevic is requesting, they are firing on the 3rd of the 472nd MTBR from the region of Libertas with mortars. Kovacevic is requesting action. He is requesting action with 130 millimetres." Do you know, which person Jovanovic is referred to there? Have you been informed or do you know who is referred to there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jovanovic, there was a Jovanovic in the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade, and I assume that this is the deputy commander of the 3rd Battalion. I assume, because there were several Jovanovics. However, since this is about what it is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what was the interpreter comment?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we have the document on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. If the document -- I'm sorry, I think we have to wait for it to be placed. Mr. Usher, we were on page 68 of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it won't be possible with the difficulties. There will be no detailed reference to it. What was read was: "Jovanovic: Kovacevic is requesting, they are firing on the 3/472 Motorised Brigade from the region of Libertas with mortars. Kovacevic is requesting action. He is requesting action with 130 mm." If you'd carry on, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sikimic, your answer about there was a Kovacevic in the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd -- Jovanovic in the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd, do you know -- if you are referring us to a person you believe was involved in the action of that day, would you know the first name of Mr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said a moment ago, one of the officers from the command of the 3rd Battalion was a Jovanovic. I cannot remember. Perhaps he was even the deputy commander. He was perhaps one of Kovacevic's deputies. Now, whether it is this Jovanovic is something that I don't know. I assume it was, but I was not there on that day so I cannot say anything with any degree of certainty. I assume that this is Captain Kovacevic's deputy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to the next entry of -- did you know -- are you aware that Captain Kovacevic's deputy was a man named Zeljko Soldo?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether he was the deputy, but he was one of Kovacevic's closest people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. May I add something. When I say I don't know with any degree of certainty, then I have to repeat what I said yesterday. I was involved in other matters. My line of work was logistics. I've forgotten some people. I've forgotten their names, perhaps. I could try to remember them, but these people and these logistics units were five, seven, or eight kilometres away behind the combat deployment, the combat order. So as for the actual deployment of these units of ours, on that line of combat, I am not aware of it in any great detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. At the entry for 10.07 on your page 68, the entry for time 10.07, "Zec called, our men are on Srdj but they are being fired upon from the town. We will now solve this and stop the fire." Do you know who "we" refers to when it says "we will now solve this and stop the fire"?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to 11.00 o'clock: "Transmitted to the ships for Lieutenant Vukmanovic, that Minister Rudolf will set sail with a ship from Gruz for the purpose of arriving for the talks. Transmitted for he 3rd of the 5th PMTBR," and then it says: "Member of the signal corps unit, Bokovic." Who was Lieutenant Vukmanovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vukmanovic was a commander, but I don't know the name of the unit that he commanded. I think it was the border unit, the 16th detachment of ships. Anyway, it was some ship-related unit. But I'm not a sailor myself, so I would not know the category of that particular unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Minister Rudolf representing the Yugoslav side or the Croatian side? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as negotiations are concerned and everything else, I have no idea about that, and I was not involved in that so I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, though, that he is associated with negotiations, Minister Rudolf? He is associated with negotiations?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You see, negotiations were conducted by a certain team which I assume was under the direct control of Admiral Jokic. So we who were engaged in other types of work did not take part in this kind of thing at all, especially I, at the time, an ordinary captain, had no contact with all of this. So I really have nothing to say in this regard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, and I wondered if maybe overnight you had a chance to think about the meaning of the abbreviations, at 11.07 we discussed the entry which said: "Stop the activities of POC"; at 11.15 stop all further actions, absolutely cease all action against the town. Transmitted to Kovacevic personally." Did you have a chance to reflect on the abbreviation POC? If not, it's okay. I just wondered if you might have.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't think about it at all. I can only repeat that in military terminology, Protivoklopna Ceta, logistics company, is abbreviated as PC, PC with a diacritic, so perhaps somebody just made a mistake of that kind, but I haven't really thought about it since.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look, please, on page 69, at the entry for 12.25: "To the command of the VPS Boka from the European mission. At 0550 hours with the fire from tanks and cannons from the positions of Strincjera, Bosanka, and Zarkovica, a machine-gun attack of the enforced infantry company has begun against the positions of the Defence Forces of the Republic of Croatia on Srdj. Along with a simultaneous opening of mortar and machine-gun fire on all parts of the town. The Defence Forces of the Republic of Croatia have responded only when the infantry and tanks have emerged 200 metres from Srdj. At the same time, we denounce any provocative acts from Srdj and Lapad which would be a cause to breach the permanent cease-fire. "We take responsibility in claiming that the allegations of our forces' actions have been constructed so as to provide an excuse for the attempt to conquer Srdj. We have also accordingly stopped further action Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. via radiogram. We expect a sincere adherence to the cease-fire and the pulling out of your forces to their initial positions. Now your forces are still acting against the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff, against Srdj, and the town of Dubrovnik." And then it says: "CS Dubrovnik." Do you know what the CS stood for, or perhaps KS in your language?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it is KS, Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to determine who had made that entry? Is that in any way evident to you from anything in the column on page 69 to the right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I really cannot say anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. On page 70 at the very top, there's a comment at 1305: "At 1400 Vice Admiral Jokic shall be at Cilipi." Do you know how far or where Cilipi is in relation to your particular command post?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think about 15 or 16 or 17 kilometres. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is it from Cavtat?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the same distance, but you go in the other direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Kumbor?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kumbor?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 40 kilometres. But I'm not sure about all of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second entry which I believe we discussed yesterday at 1305, but perhaps -- and you were not able to --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You helped us yesterday. We'll go on, on that one.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look down, please, to 1415 on page 70.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The entry at 1415 says: "The helicopter with the commander has taken off from the Cilipi airport to Belgrade." Now, does that link up in any way in your view to what was said at 1305 above? Was the commander -- that's Vice Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please turn to page 71. And before I ask you about page 71, if I were to suggest to you that POC refers to -- now, forgive my pronunciation perhaps, Protivoklopna Ceta, does that make sense to you? Anti-tank company? Does that sound like it might be what the abbreviation could be?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Looking at page 71, the entry for 1538: "Dubrovnik Crisis Staff; at 6.12 at 1515 hours, at 1515 the Old Town centre of Dubrovnik is in flames. We are requesting an urgent cease-fire so that we could locate the fires." Then there is a name Zeljko Sikic. Do you know or had you ever heard of a person Zeljko Sikic before in any of the communications you may have been involved in?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At 1540 on page 71: "For the Crisis Staff, our forces have ceased fire on all parts of Dubrovnik at 1245. We absolutely reject the possibility that our forces are acting during the alleged time, and especially on the Old Town. According to our information, the positions on Petka are fired upon from Kolocep," and it shows "VPS Boka." Do we interpret this as the sender, the originator of the message is, someone at VPS Boka?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We can interpret it in the following way: That this information was sent with this content by the party that could send a telegram of this nature. And in principle, one knows who can communicate with the other side, the other party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in principle, who would that be in your view?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been only three men, three officers: Admiral Jokic, his deputy, and the chief of the operations centre, Kozaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could look at 1600 -- the entry for 1600 on page 71, says: "Dubrovnik Crisis Staff: VPS Boka Lieutenant General Strugar from Minister Rudolf. "Comrade general from 0545 of the morning hours until present 1530, the firing on Dubrovnik continues as I write this. The town has suffered fierce attacks from various directions and is greatly damaged, and especially the sacral objects. The Orthodox church is presently on fire as well as houses on five locations. Dubrovnik is faced with the danger of being engulfed in a wider fire. Bearing in mind that there is no water, it is impossible to put out the flames. Two are killed, 17 people wounded. We request that you momentarily cease fire on Dubrovnik." I'm not sure if "momentarily" is the correct translation. But: "Momentarily cease fire on Dubrovnik because the consequences are incomprehensible and our interventions minimal. We emphasise that the hit Franciscan monastery is an object which is clearly identified by the C or SK. We expect your intervention and primarily your response." Is there any indication who received that message or made that entry? You don't see any indication, do you? There's nothing there that indicates?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a message, is it not, this is clearly a message from Mr. Rudolf to General Strugar, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. Objection, Your Honour. Because that is not what it says here. When the document is shown, the document should be read out. It says: "Crisis Staff Dubrovnik -- for VPS Boka, and then Lieutenant Colonel Strugar." That is what it says here, so that is how it has to be put to the witness. So VPS Boka, General Strugar. That is what is written here, and that is the only way the question can be phrased by quoting accurately what the document actually says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: VPS Boka, was that not the recipient of messages for General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All messages went through the VPS. The operations centre of the VPS Boka. So whoever called from anywhere had to go through the operations centre of Boka, not through the forward command post. There was no direct communication between the forward command post and General Strugar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so this message --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So a message for General Strugar would end up in this format? This is a normal way to send a message to General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This message arrived in this document, I assume, because the commander or his deputy, that is to say, Admiral Jokic, or warship Captain Zec were probably in this zone. And that is why the message arrived in Kupari because it is customary for the message to come where the commander is, or rather where his deputy is. And this is a message from the Crisis Staff which was conveyed to one of our commanders. What the answer was, how the answer was given, who gave the answer, that is something that I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The indication is that it is addressed to General Strugar. Do you see his name there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what it says here, that this message should be conveyed to General Strugar, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you would look at page 72, please, the entry there -- under 1627, there are two parts to it, if you can see it. In the top part, and then there's a second part which starts: "Crisis Staff Dubrovnik, for KVPS Boka." And that's the part I'm going to ask you about. "In your radiogram from 1440 hours in which you erroneously claim that you have ceased fire on all parts of Dubrovnik since 1115 hours, not only have we convinced ourselves in this untruthfulness but also the representatives of UNICEF, UNESCO, and the EM. We once more ask for your guarantee that you will cease the cannon and MB fire, so that we could commence putting out the flames in the old part of town he. We also expect that you will stop the action against Srdj." And then it says: "Op Dubrovnik Crisis Staff." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. What does the Op, the O-p Dubrovnik Crisis Staff mean, if you know?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. KS Dubrovnik, that stands for Crisis Staff Dubrovnik. As for your O-p, I don't know what that stands for. I really don't know. For the reasons I gave a moment ago, I absolutely had no part in this, so that the normal wording KS Dubrovnik must stand for the Crisis Staff, but I don't know about the rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the entry for 1835, at the very bottom, it says: "The team of the 2nd Operational Group, captain of warship Milanovic, Colonel Andzic, and Dr. Antic." Then it says: "Team of 9th VPS, Captain Kozaric, Zarkovic, Jeremic, for the inspection of the situation in the 3/472 MTBR." What are these various persons listed next to team of the 2nd Operational Group? Do you know Milanovic, Andzic, and Dr. Antic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- you've mentioned Captain Kozaric before, so you know him.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Zarkovic, do you know? Zarkovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was one of the assistant commanders of the naval sector. I think he was responsible for morale, but I'm not sure. As for Jeremic, I'm not sure at all. There were two or three persons with that surname. I think that one of the Jeremics did take part in the negotiations, but I cannot tell you for certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, I do know Captain Kozaric, battleship commander Zarkovic. Him I know as well. The two of them I know personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would look at -- if you would turn the page to page 73, please, the entry for 1840: "According to the report of the captain of the battleship or warship Celebic, there are five dead and eight wounded." Did you come to learn who the five dead and eight wounded were? Or are they referring to who's dead, who's wounded? Do you know? Were you ever made aware?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know -- may I give a slightly lengthier explanation. When I handed over duty at 0630, I went to carry out another assignment. And I wasn't at the operations centre. Throughout that day, I am aware that there were some reconnoitering, that there was a lot of problems, to put it that way. But all I can say is that I did hear from colleagues, from comrades that day that on our side there were five or six dead, a couple wounded, and that everything is being looked into, investigated, and addressed in a certain manner. I'm not even sure of the actual numbers. But I did hear, since I was thereabouts, although I was doing something else, that there were five or six dead and some wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "on that day," which day are you referring to? Could you give us the date of the day you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 6th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to discuss anything that you might have known about any of the events that occurred between the 5th and the 6th of December? Were you ever asked formally by any commanding officer?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we look back at page 73, at the entry for 1922, a message for Lieutenant General Strugar from Dubrovnik. "Rudolf: Because the fire is burning in the old centre of Dubrovnik and threatening with horrible consequences due to the lack of water, we ask that you enable the entry of ships with water cannons whose purpose is to extinguish the fires from Korcula, Ploce, into the old harbour of Dubrovnik. It is an urgent and necessary intervention. We expect your initial consent after which we would precisely inform you of the type of ships and their time of arrival." And there appears the name: "Minister Davorin Rudolf." Do you find on page 73 any indication as to who may have made that notation?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 73 towards the bottom, the time is indicated, 2010. And on the right-hand side, there's initial. Let me say again that I assume that it is of Frigate Captain Kozaric. There are no other notes as regards any earlier entries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the entry for 1930 for the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff: "Lieutenant-General Pavle Strugar gives his initial consent for the arrival of the ships, tugboats with water cannons into the old harbour of Dubrovnik in order to extinguish the fires. Please inform us timely of the ship's number so as to ensure their unimpeded passage." And then it says at the bottom of the message: "Lieutenant General Pavle Strugar."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the document be adjusted on the ELMO for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I am afraid I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I hadn't finished it yet. There was an intervention by the interpreters. When it says at the bottom of the message Lieutenant General Pavle Strugar, that indicates that message is sent by Lieutenant General Pavle Strugar, does it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't claim that. I do know that someone from the forward command post or rather the basic command post returned that message for the Crisis Staff of Dubrovnik. Now, whether prior to that there was an approval received from General Strugar or not, I can't claim. But that such a message was sent, that is what is indicated here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does it appear to you -- it does appear to you, doesn't it, that this message at 1930 is a response to a message at 1922 from Minister Rudolf to General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please take a look at page 74. The entry at 2210: "Dubrovnik Crisis Staff. As a consequence of today's shelling, there are fires over the entire city and on the island of Lokrum. For the purpose of locating the places caught by fire on the island of Lokrum, we ask that you enable the unimpeded and safe passage both to and from Lokrum which will be organised during this night, the night of 6th and 7th of December. We ask your consent and urgent response." And then it says: "Asked Celebic. He told me to decide for myself." Are you able to determine from the entries there who asked Celebic and who ended up having to decide for himself?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's quite certain that whoever wrote this or received this message from the Crisis Staff could not -- actually he noted this down, that he had asked this Celebic. So I'm afraid I can't know who Celebic is and where he was because I really don't know that. I'm not familiar with the name at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Would you look at page 75, please. The entry for 1002: "Urgent telegram for Admiral Jokic (in person). According to confidential information, ones who do not want peace in this region are planning to jeopardise the negotiations and thus the lives of the negotiators are endangered. We therefore suggest that the negotiations should take place at sea near Cavtat on a ship either yours or ours. We will arrive with a ship Arka who belongs to the Dubrovnik company Atlas. We will thus arrive from the Gruz harbour via the south side of the Lokrum island and we will arrive at Cavtat or rather at your ship. We ask that you assure the safety of the ship Arka's voyage to the rendezvous location and back. The ship will set sail under the flag of the EC." And under the message is the name Davorin Rudolf. Are you able to determine who made that particular entry? Is it at all clear to you from anything?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no really not. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look down at the entry for 1035 on that same page: "KVPS Boka to be delivered to Admiral Jokic in person. In relation to our radiogram from this morning due to the damage to the ship Arka which was discovered just now, we are forced to substitute the same with the ship called Krila Dubrovnika, wings of Dubrovnik. We ask you to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. ensure its safe and free voyage under the flag of UNICEF from the Gruz harbour via the south side of Lokrum island until Cavtat, i.e., until we arrive at your ship and back. I ask for your urgent response. Davorin Rudolf." Is it evident at all who may have been responsible for that particular message being entered there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If you could look at page 76, please, at the entry for 1052: "For the Crisis Staff Dubrovnik, Davorin Rudolf. We accept your suggestion to arrive with the motorboat Krila Dubrovnika. Since there as a storm in the region of Cavtat, it would be difficult to hold the talks on the ship. We recommend that you dock at the Cavtat harbour, i.e., Srebrno where we will greet you and hold the talks. We will ensure the safety of the ship from the Srebrno harbour and back as well as your own personal safety. Command VPS Boka." Is there any indication from anything that you see on that page who took that message in?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the indication of the command of VPS Boka, to whom do you believe that would be referring?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, to the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose name was?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Admiral Jokic. It couldn't imply anyone else but the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at 1135: "Dubrovnik Crisis Staff, in relation to your radiogram received at 1110 hours we hereby confirm the arrival to Srebreno." It bears the name -- that message has Davorin Rudolf. Any indication of who would have taken that one down from anything you see on that page?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I'd rather not engage in any guesswork.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at 1535: "Colonel Panic was informed that based upon the statement of Captain Kovacevic, there is no fire in Dubrovnik." Who was Colonel Panic, if you know?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not at the forward command post in Kupari so that I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we go -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me a minute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll just have a look at an earlier page and ask you a quick question, couple of questions. On page 63, please, do you have that in front of you? Page 63.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at the entry for 1220, and it looks like -- the English says: "K1 K1 Knezevic, message from the Dubrovnik Crisis Staff: We protest against the action of your units from the region of old Bosanka who are shooting with snipers at the Old Town where two civilians were wounded at 1100 hours. We expect that you will prevent the arbitrary acts of some of your units whereby you would solve the breach of the cease-fire, signed unconditionally, and thus save the lives of the civilians of Dubrovnik." And then it bears the words "Dubrovnik Crisis Staff." Now, is it -- do you see -- what date is that referring to, if we go back a little bit? Are you able to take a look and identify the date?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 5th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help us, please, understand what this -- it looks like K1 K1 Knezevic. What does that mean? Is that a name?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A customary abbreviation for Captain First Class is this, Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a person you knew of Captain First Class Knezevic associated with either the op centre or the headquarters or...

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the operations centre of the forward command post in Kupari, there was no such person of that name with that rank. My interpretation would be that this is a message that was received in Kumbor because I mentioned a moment ago that everything went through the Kumbor operations centre where the communications were. So someone, as there's no initial or signature on the right-hand side, someone at 1220 noted down a message from Captain First Class Knezevic which reads as follows. So Captain First Class Knezevic conveyed this message, and that is why it was entered here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at page 66. At the entry for 2355, that is referring to 2355 on the 5th of December. Now, your shift started at --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your shift began at midnight, did it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did you actually physically find yourself in the operations centre? Were you there before midnight?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how much --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If necessary, I can give a more detailed answer. I said yesterday that most of the activities took place at the operations centre so that a lot of time was spent there. It was known who was on duty when that person would take over. However, the rest of the time we were also at the operations centre or nearby. So I can claim with certainty that I had been there much earlier than that as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you there when this message at 2355 was taken in, where it says: "Captain Kovacevic, we have cast light towards Srdj, and they are opening fire on us. What shall I do? We have responded to him that he should withhold fire unless their action endangers the lives of the soldiers. He has recommended that a protest should be filed and thereby to direct their attention not to act from Srdj." Were you there when that message came in?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume I was. And I must have been as I would take over my shift at 2400 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- was it part of your role, or it was part of your role, was it not, as duty officer taking on a shift to be briefed by the outgoing duty officer to know what had happened or what events might have been occurring in the previous shift?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you informed of anything that would have caused you particular alarm or concern when you took over this shift from your predecessor?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know or was it explained to you what is said in this message? "We have responded to him that he should hold -- sorry, "that he should withhold fire." Do you know who the "we" is in that message? Are you able to help us with that? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operations centre of the forward command post at Kupari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they are able to make certain decisions on the spot based on the circumstances, the situation? They're able to -- I'm sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Absolutely yes, because this was a customary measure that would be applied for some time. There are certain instructions that everyone at the operations centre is guided by and no special permission is required from a superior to say not to jeopardise Dubrovnik, not to open fire on Dubrovnik. So the established instructions were not to open fire and to protect the civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can I ask you, please, to turn the page to something that's called -- it looks like an overview of events. At least, that's the translation that we have in English. And I'm trying to see where it would be -- yeah, overview in English. It doesn't have a page number, but it follows page 66. Who makes -- I mean, isn't it the responsibility of the duty officer as you have indicated to make entries? Who would make overviews of events? Why would you be doing that? Or rather, who does that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A recapitulation or overview of events of the previous day is done by the chief of the operations centre, Kozaric or his deputy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in this overview of events that is there, if you look at the entry, for example -- the comment, it says, from 745 to 830: "Kovacevic has requested support from the 3rd of the 5th PMTBR. They are not informing us, rather the commander of the 3 of the 5th PMTBR pursuant to the earlier decisions is opening fire on," and then it lists various locations including Lazaret, Hotel Neptune, Nuncijata, Sustjepan. Are you able to tell us anything you're aware of from your shift the night before, anything that you know that would have seemed to lead - at least from your shift - to lead to this type of activity? Anything that you were personally aware of from what happened on your shift that would have led to this type of opening of fire on various areas, just from your shift?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, because everything was peaceful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, there were two exhibits yesterday that my learned friends opposite asked you about. One was D97, if I could just ask for a recap of that. Just to save you steps, I'm asking about D97 and D98, if it would make the walk shorter. The two documents, let's take a look first just in order, D97, which is dated the 4th of December, 1991. I think it was described as just a logistics order, something in the normal course. It says: "To the command of the 2nd Operational Group and the command of the VPO IKM." That indicates, does it not, that that was addressed to both formations, to the 2nd Operational Group command and the command of the 9th VPS. Is that right? Yes -- could you --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at D98, please, D98, which is a document from the 5th of December. Do you have that in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That also does it not indicate that it is addressed to the command of the VPO, which the military sector -- I'm sorry, district. And the command of the 2nd Operational Group. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. One last question I wanted to inquire of relating to something you commented on earlier. Oh, I'm so sorry. Those two -- I think perhaps you may have helped us, and I don't want to repeat. Petar Dragicevic signed off on both of those orders. Now, you indicated he was an assistant commander for logistics. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petar Dragicevic, yes. A colonel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just want to look at one other entry. You had indicated from page 68 of the document that's called a war diary, there's an entry at page 68 at 9.00 o'clock. We discussed it yesterday. If you could take a quick look?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it says: "Precisely determine who and when opened fire. Captain Kovacevic is to write a statement to the commander." Did you ever see a statement by Captain Kovacevic to the commander?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, which command --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on the way this message is written, is it clear to you or evident to you which commander is referred to here? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The immediately subordinate person was Captain Kovacevic. So the reference is to Admiral Jokic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, thank you very much. At the time, we have finished our cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Somers. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Petrovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few questions, sir. Can you please look at the document that we call the war diary, and can you please look at the entry for 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And what date are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 6th, page 70.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The time is 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says here: "Captain Kovacevic is thinking about withdrawing his men because they're exhausted. It is cold. He has been ordered to make a decision as to what he is supposed to do." Can you please look at this signature. Do you recognise it, the signature on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is the signature of Captain Kozaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a message that Captain Kozaric --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I don't know how given that there are discrete entries, but if redirect happens to touch on areas specifically from cross, this particular entry was not asked about in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's correct. The question has been asked and answered. I hope you'll ensure that your re-examination deals with matters raised during cross-examination, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with all due respect, I believe that my learned friend was asking questions about a document and about the entry relative to the 6th of December and the entries which are relative to the person whose name is Kozaric. On several occasions, she put a question about the entries for which the witness believed that they were entries signed by Captain Kozaric. And I'm doing the same thing. I'm asking him questions about the entry which was supposed to be entered by Captain Kozaric, and that's why, Your Honours, I would like you to give me the permission to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, Mr. Petrovic. You're going to different entries. There was no apparent connection in the purpose or the entry. So that's going beyond the proper realm of re-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sikimic, can you please look at page 68, and the entry was made at 950.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you mentioned in answering my questions the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade, the unit led by Zdravkovic, is this Jovanovic who is a member of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I told you that I didn't know any such person. I know that there were men called Jovanovic in the 3rd and in the 2nd unit. Now, who is this referring to? I don't know. I told you already that I couldn't be sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at -- and let's limit ourselves to the entries made on the 6th of December between pages 67 and 75. I'm going to put several questions to you now. Can you please look at page 69 first. The entry made at 1255 -- 1225. And it was sent to the command of the Military Naval District Boka by the European Monitoring Mission. Can you please look immediately after that entry which was made at 1225. Is there anywhere, an entry showing that this message sent by the European Monitoring Mission was indeed forwarded to the command of the 2nd Operations Group after this entry which was made at 1225? Please look if there is an entry showing that the operations centre of the military naval district indeed forwarded this message to the operations group?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, can you please look at page 71, the entry which was made at 1600 hours.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a message of the Crisis Staff from Dubrovnik to the Military Naval District of Boka. And after this entry at 1600 hours, is there another entry showing that the message which was obviously received by the military naval district was forwarded to the command of the 2nd Operations Group?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that you can't see it or there's no entry? Please look at the page carefully. You have enough time. Can you please find such an entry.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no such an indication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now can you please look at page 72. This is an entry made at 1627 hours, actually beneath that entry the Crisis Staff of Dubrovnik, and the message was sent to the KVPS Boka. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is the command of the Military Naval District of Boka. After that, can you look at the other entries, is there an indication that this command was ever forwarded to the command of the 2nd Operations Group? Can you please look at the page carefully.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at page 73. The entry made at 1922, for Lieutenant General Strugar from Mr. Rudolf; we assume it is from Mr. Rudolf. Can you please look at the entries that follow the entry at 1922. Do you see an indication that this message was indeed forwarded to the command of the 2nd Operations Group?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The message is addressed to the 2nd OG. There's no indication that you have to have proof of forwarding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think the intervention is appropriate at the present time. Carry on, Mr. Petrovic. But you might inquire whether this is a record of all signals sent or merely a record of important issues. To illustrate my point, Mr. Petrovic, the very message you're looking at 1922, there is no indication of that being forwarded. Yet, at 1930, there is a reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The entry that was made at 1922, is there an indication that it was forwarded to the 2nd Operations Group? Is there an entry showing that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no entry. Whether it was or whether it wasn't, I can't say in view of what I can see beneath this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Is this an important message? Because it was a message that was sent by a minister in the government of the Republic of Croatia. Would such a message have to be forwarded to the person that it was addressed to?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can we see here that this was done? Is there a trace of this being done?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there isn't, and I don't know why as in principle, it should have been forwarded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since all the communications are entered in the war diary, if this message had been forwarded to the 2nd Operations Group, would this have been recorded in the war diary?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the entry made at 1930 hours. If an answer had arrived from General Strugar or a comment made on his part to the forward command post of the 9th VPS, would that message be recorded?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I just give you comments on what I can see here. At 1930, the person who made the entry wrote that this was a message for the Crisis Staff. Who was it who delivered the message? Was this a written message, an oral message, I really wouldn't be able to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you the following: If General Pavle Strugar as the commander of the 2nd Operations Group had sent a message or some sort of communication to the operations centre or to the forward command post of the 9th VPS, would such a message be recorded in this war log?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before this entry at 1930 hours, is there another entry relative to communication between the VPS and the command of the 2nd Operations Group relative to the letter that was sent at 1922?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before this entry at 1930, is there any indication that General Strugar or the 2nd Operations Group had communication with the forward command post of the 9th VPS and ordered for the message with this content to be forwarded to the Crisis Staff of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any document to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If General Strugar had indeed sent any message --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This is going well beyond the scope of cross-examination. This is a new re-examination -- a new direct examination. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it is a reaction to my intervention at this point. I could observe, Mr. Petrovic, that looking through the whole of this, it seems to me that it is clearly not a record of all messages received and sent. So I let you know that. You'll see no end of inward messages; you'll see responses at a later time, and clearly there has been communication, decision in between. All that is recorded is the original request and the ultimate answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with all due respect, the Defence believes that there was no communication at all, that everything that happened, happened at the level of the forward command post of the 9th VPS without anything being forwarded to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... this is argument made in front of a witness. It can colour the response. It's inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's my fault. I think you're quite right, Ms. Somers. But I felt it better to let Mr. Petrovic my reaction to this document. It's merely my present reaction, and it's only my personal one. So that he can be aware of that in his further re-examination because the matter does appear to be of some significance to the Defence. Now, you may, of course, now continue with your re-examination, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you observe the normal rules as to re-examination. And it may be that you'll be able to deal with the matter that I've raised in some way. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sikimic, my question -- my general question with regard to all of these entries is as follows: If there had been communication between the forward command post of the 9th VPS and the command of the 2nd Operations Group, bearing in mind the significance of such communication, would any such message have to be entered in the war log of the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I don't have any further questions. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you still have in front of you the MFI D96, the original document? I think the witness may have it.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're talking about the war log, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Could you turn to page 67. Not on the ELMO, thank you.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I just wonder if you would help me by reading the entry at 0715, 0-7-1-5.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 0705? I apologise. Did you say 0705?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 15. The entry reads: "Zoljas and 82-millimetre shells around 0600 from Srdj. The positions on Strincjera were shelled."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. What are Zoljas?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zolja is a weapon used to destroy armoured vehicles and other equipment and troops. But mostly, it is used to destroy armoured vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Normally armour-piercing shells. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at 0745, could you read the entry there, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't. The first word is: "Order the company to get ready to intervene." To the medical company, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise, SNC would be the proper way of putting it, but it is just SN company. So I suppose that is that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. That's the way it has been translated in English, and it didn't make any sense to me. But you think it's the medical company?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I have a small question for you. On the same page at 050, there is an entry saying that the 3rd Battalion of the 5th is not responding. And my question is, did any action -- was any action taken in regard of this? Or was it just assumed that their communication facilities didn't work?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No action was taken in this regard. At that moment, they did not respond, and they did not send their report. There must have been subsequent communication because there were no problems at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SIKIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you switched on? Sorry, we don't get a red light on that, and it appears you're not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems, Your Honour, that the red light it off for the Defence at the moment. My request --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... if you're not getting a red signal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid, Your Honour, to come to any optimistic conclusions. I'm never prone to jump to any optimistic conclusions. Your Honour, with regard to the scope of the cross-examination by my learned friend with regard to this document which is marked as D96, can this document be admitted as a Defence exhibit? If, Your Honour, you still believe there are things to be clarified with regard to this document, I would kindly ask for your concrete instructions as to what is being expected from the Defence in terms of laying foundations for this document to be admitted as per Rule 79(C). Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I ask the Chamber to focus its attention on page 72 of the document, please. There's an entry at 1605 that says: "KK Stojadinovic has reported that Rodos II could not enter," et cetera, et cetera. If the Chamber at its earliest opportunity could take a look in the transcript of 19th April 2004 at page 4925, line 14, cross-examination by Mr. Rodic, the question: "Do you know that at 1605, Captain Stojadinovic informed the forward command post that because of the crossfire at the Croatian forces Petka, Lapad, Kolocep, the ship Rodos" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I apologise. Let me start again for the interpreters. "Do you know that at 1605 Captain Stojadinovic informed the forward command post that because of the crossfire of the Croatian forces Petka, Lapad, Kolocep, the ship Rodos II could not sail into Dubrovnik. Is it an officer of the 9th VPS who was reporting about this what is called internal conflict among the Croatian forces?" This is a very specific reference which happens to appear in the document called war diary, MFI 96. If the Chamber for a moment could direct its attention to page 66 of MFI 96, and where the entry for 25 -- I'm sorry, 2355 goes, the reference is to: "We have responded to him that he should withhold fire unless their action," et cetera, et cetera. If at its convenience the Chamber may look at the transcript for -- yes, in the cross-examination of Admiral Jokic by Mr. -- I'm sorry. No, I don't have a correct cite for that. I'm terribly sorry. What I just referred to you, I strike that. I apologise, I had the wrong citation. But what I refer to you earlier was the cross-examination of Admiral Jokic. And the specificity of the question suggests strongly that a document was in the possession of the Defence, at least at that time, or at least the information sufficiently detailed in such a way as to have put whatever questions may have been appropriate to Admiral Jokic, the commander of the 9th VPS, and obviously a very highly relevant person with regard to the incidents there. I'm confident with more time, I would be able to comb the record and find more. But accordingly, our objection from yesterday as to the 90(H) (ii) violation stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider over the break the question of the admissibility of MFI D96. In the meantime, Mr. Sikimic, may we thank you for your assistance. You'll be pleased to know your evidence is at an end, and you're now free to return to your duties. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the first break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The next witness could be brought in while we note our decision in respect of MFI D96. We have noted the objections and the explanation that during cross-examination, in particular, of Admiral Jokic, the Defence counsel had only notes made from an examination of the war diary, a request to be provided with a copy of it not having at that time been complied with, and that now they do have relevant copies from the war diary. From a quick overview of the cross-examination where it is clear that an attempt was made to deal with material differences between the case for the Defence and the evidence of the admiral insofar as these were drawn from the war diary, the Chamber is of the view that MFI D96 should become an exhibit. We hardly need say that the question of what weight will be attached to individual parts of it remains very much to be determined in the light of all the evidence which in the end will tell upon the war diary and the matters that are recorded in it so that it remains as with other evidence subject to the eventual assessment of weight by the Trial Chamber. So that document may now be recorded as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Exhibit Number is D96.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If you will take the card given to you now and read aloud the affirmation, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Rodic:

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even the signal lamp on the microphone works now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you kindly introduce yourself to us with your full name and surname.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I am Zoran Lemal, born on the 5th of August, 1966 in Sremska Mitrovica. My father's name is Janika, and my mother's name is Nevenka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we start the examination-in-chief, I will like to draw your attention to the following: We speak the same language, so after my question, could you pause briefly, and then start your answer so that we would not speak at the same time because all of this has to be interpreted. Could you please tell me where you live now and what you do.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I live in Sremska Mitrovica, and I work as an active-duty officer in the garrison in Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what is your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I am an ethnic Hungarian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in 1991 where were you -- or rather, were you in active military service?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: In 1991, I was in active service at the school centre of the infantry in Bileca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your duty there? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I was commanding officer of a platoon in the battalion for training cadets at the reserve officers' school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what is your education? What schools have you completed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I completed the military high school called Brotherhood and Unity in Belgrade, and the military academy, the land forces department, the infantry division.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you serve in Bileca throughout 1991 or were there any changes involved?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I did not serve in Bileca all the time. Sometime in mid-September, the infantry administration ordered me to work temporarily in the 472nd Brigade of the marine infantry in Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you indeed report at the 472nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I reported sometime between the 23rd and the 25th of September to the commander of the brigade, Colonel Obrad Vicic, who assigned me further to the 3rd Battalion to work for Captain First Class Ekrem Devlic. I was commander of the 2nd Company within that battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know who the commander of that brigade was before Obrad Vicic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I know who the commander of that brigade was. It was Colonel Nojko Marinovic who had left that unit and went to Dubrovnik. It was after that that Colonel Vicic took over the command of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any comments within your brigade in relation to the fact that the former commander, Nojko Marinovic, left the brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Upon arriving in that unit and assuming my duties, most of the reserve personnel who were supposed to be mobilised in that unit did not respond to call-up because they were from the area of Dubrovnik. And that is why it was from Trebinje, Bileca, Gacko that the brigade was manned by reserve personnel. And there were quite a few protests because the commander Nojko Marinovic had left the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, at that time, what was the attitude of those people towards you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Since Colonel Nojko Marinovic left the unit, since he was an ethnic Croat, and I came as a company leader to that battalion and I'm an ethnic Hungarian, at first, there was some skepticism as far as I was concerned. I was suspected. And anyway, everybody in that unit was very cautious as far as I was concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already mentioned this problem with manning the brigade due to the fact that reservists from Dubrovnik did not answer the call-up. Were there any problems regarding the manning of the unit in terms of the military specialties that were required, the VES?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: There were even more problems in that respect because people were not trained, they did not have the appropriate VES. Quite simply, units were manned in order to meet certain numeric levels, but not much attention was paid to VES selection. It was not possible anyway because most of the people who were trained for particular activities did not respond to the call-up because, as we already said, they were from the Dubrovnik area. So we had to focus on training the personnel as much as we could so that they could use the weapons that they were assigned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when you reported at the Trebinje Brigade and when you were assigned to the 2nd Company of the 3rd Battalion, were you sent to a particular position or place?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I reported to brigade headquarters in Trebinje, and that's where Colonel Vicic was and Major Radovan Komar, Chief of Staff. They provided transportation for me so that I could go to the command post of the commander of the battalion that was within the area of the village of Hum. I established contact with Captain First Class Ekrem Devlic there, and he told me where my unit was. And from there, together with me, he went to the deployment area of the 2nd Company where I established contact with Reserve Captain Gasic, who was commander of the company until then, and I took over the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know when combat activities started in 1991, the ones that your unit took part in?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Well, I would not call that combat activity that we took part in because we were given the assignment to move from the then position to the positions in the area of Ivanica where weekend cottages were. And on the 1st of October, we were shelled by Croat forces from the area of Kupari. This was at Gornji Ivanica. This was on the 1st of October. Eight soldiers were killed in that attack. These soldiers were from the anti-tank company. They belonged to Captain Nesic. I did not sustain any losses in my own unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you know how these men were killed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: It happened in the following way: When we came to Ivanica where weekend cottages were, we took up positions for the units, and the anti-tank unit was put on the very outskirts of Ivanica whereas the others were deployed -- the other units were deployed in the interior. So that unit was visible from the area of Konavle, from the Dubrovnik area down there from Kupari. Most probably this was the reason why these positions were targeted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps what kind of fire was opened at that unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Mortar fire was opened at the positions of our battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this incident, did these units remain at the same positions? Or were they redeployed elsewhere? Specifically, your battalion.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: After these events, there was a dispersion of units from that area. In fact, withdrawal in order to rest in a different area. I specifically went to the Golubov Kamen position and the ridge above Rijeka Dubrovacka. The other units were also deployed elsewhere because the entire battalion was concentrated there in Ivanica where the weekend cottages were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask the usher for his assistance. Could the witness please be given P134. This is a map dated the 2nd of December, 1991. I'm sorry, P132.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, can you see Trebinje on this map?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the map please be moved a bit to the left. Fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please point Trebinje out for us.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you? Could you indicate where you were on the 1st of October when these soldiers were killed.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the area?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: This is the area of the weekend cottages, Ivanica. And it is close to the Trebinje-Dubrovnik Road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate now what positions you took up after the 1st of October.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I left the area of Ivanica on orders, and I took up the positions of Golubov Kamen above the source of Dubrovacka Rijeka [as interpreted] and the ridge itself, above Rijeka Dubrovacka, together with my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, during the month of October, did your unit take part in any combat activity?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: During the month of October, our unit did not take part in any other combat activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the month of October 1991, did you take part in any military action?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I did. This happened on the 23rd of October in an area that can be seen here on this map. That is to say, from Ivanica towards Gornji Brgat, the ridge there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The commander of the battalion together with his reconnaissance squad went out to reconnoiter there. He was ambushed there, together with his command, and five soldiers were killed. And the commander of the battalion himself was wounded. They remained sealed off there near a wall closer to Gornji Brgat rather than to Ivanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, who opened fire at them and from where?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Fire was opened at them from the area of the village of Gornji Brgat, from the area of the village of Donji Brgat, and the village of Martinovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you to be able to see all that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I was given an assignment by the deputy battalion commander, Captain Vladimir Kovacevic, together with a platoon to head in the direction that the battalion commander had been reconnoitering and to pull him out and the men who were with him from that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did that look like? Did you find the dead and wounded?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: As we moved, I was also shot at from the same positions that they were fired at as I have indicated. There were quite a number of anti-infantry mines on the ridge, on the left- and right-hand side. To the left was the highway, and to the right was the old railway line leading to Dubrovnik so that our movement was rather slow because we had to remove the mines that we came across. I found them, and I got in touch with Captain Devlic, who was on the other side of the wall, and I asked him whether he could see where the fire was coming from because the shooting continued at the wall which prevented us from crossing it. He answered that they were shooting from the tower [as interpreted] in the village in Brgat because he was the only one who was at the level of the ridge where we were. Then I led the soldiers down the ridge to the left and the right, and then we managed to pass through an opening in the wall to the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in connection with the transcript, on page 42, line 3, it says: "From the tower in the village in Brgat." The word "church" is missing. It should be church tower in the village of Brgat. That is what the witness said, and this can be checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the battalion commander who was wounded informed you where the fire was coming from, were you able to see that position?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just beg your pardon for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May that -- Could that be clarified from the witness, whether the witness in fact said "church."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there more than one tower in the village of Brgat? Perhaps you could clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, you have described the situation that fire was opened at you and that you couldn't cross the wall. What exactly did you ask the battalion commander and what exactly did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: As I was on the side of the wall that was closer to the holiday village Ivanica whereas the commander and the killed soldiers were on the side that was closer to the village of Brgat, I asked him whether he could see the positions from which fire was being opened by the enemy forces because it was very risky to peep over the wall for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did the commander tell you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: He answered that they were shooting from houses in the village of Donji Brgat, the lateral side of that ridge. And along the way that we were going, they were opening fire from the church tower because he had noticed fire coming from that same position directed at them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After receiving that information from the battalion commander, did you, too, look in the direction of that church?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I was saying that we were going slightly downhill to the left so that we couldn't be seen from the church tower. And we passed through the wall without further problems, and we headed forward toward the commander and the soldiers. But we were very cautious regarding the church tower. Having reached the ridge where they were, I separated the machine-gun operator and a sniper who covered the church tower so that we were able to pull out the commander and the wounded soldiers to the other side of the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, during this pull-out operation, were there any other casualties on your side?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: There were. When we had crossed to the other side of the wall, they started shelling us with hand-held launchers and machine-gun fire was intensified from the area of Donji Brgat so that as a result of all this, a soldier of mine was shot, and he died, Miroslav Anusic who came from Backa Palanka. I, too, was hit by a hand-held rocket launcher, and I had minor injuries in the spine area and the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you manage to complete your operation of evacuating the wounded?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. The operation was completed. We pulled out all the dead and all the wounded who were there. And we managed to get back to the Ivanica holiday home settlement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in connection with this operation, was any -- were any of the participants in the operation praised or rewarded or decorated?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. In connection with this operation, soldier Anusic, Miroslav Anusic, was posthumously awarded a medal of courage, and I also received a medal of courage, as did soldier Pantic, Saka, who removed the mines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the usher to assist me in distributing a document, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what kind of document it is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
