utterances.text: It is a decree of the Presidency of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia number 53 dated the 25th of November, 1991 whereby for demonstrating personal courage and the dedication in the saving of human lives and supplies, I was decorated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this -- did this decoration come as a result of the operation you took part in?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would ask to tender this document into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D99.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Lemal, please, after you were wounded in this operation, did you undergo treatment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I spent seven days in the hospital in Trebinje. I was hospitalised there. And after that, for another 15 days, I was treated at home in my apartment in Bileca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So about 20 or 21 days, you were absent from your unit. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were recovering, did you know where your unit was located and what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how it was that you knew?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: In the unit itself, I had a large number of reserve -- reservists from Bileca and Gacko. One of them was Sergeant Sreten Nikolic from Gacko who would pass through Bileca on his way home and he would drop in to see me. And he would inform of me about the position of our company and our battalion, so that at all times I knew where my unit was located while I was absent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you returned to the unit in mid-November. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, from Sreten Nikolic or any other member of your unit, did you hear that your unit had taken part in any combat during November?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: After these events of the 23rd of October, the unit was withdrawn to rest in Hum. And afterwards, after this period of rest, I learned that they were involved in combat operations to capture Donji Brgat, Zarkovica, and the village of Bosanka, and the entire plateau overlooking the town of Dubrovnik. And that in those battles, the unit behaved well and that they were praised by the superior command for the courage and initiative they had shown in combat operations to capture these territories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you which the superior command was to your unit.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The superior command to that unit was the naval sector or region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear what positions your battalion took up, if any, in November 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about it. All that I have mentioned was taken control of. First, the village of Donji Brgat, then the attack continued in the direction of the village of Bosanka, Zarkovica, the Kula Graci and Kula Strincjera. These were the facilities that were captured. The only facility that was not captured in that attack was the Srdj relay station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any casualties? Did you hear whether there were any casualties in your unit during these combat operations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: As far as I know, there weren't any losses in my company. As for the other companies, I'm not sure about that. But I think that they didn't have any losses either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you pulled out the wounded battalion commander Devlic on the 23rd of October, did he continue to be the commander of 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade, or were there any changes made?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I returned around the middle of November to the battalion. And at the command post in the village of Gornji Brgat, which had been captured by then, I found Captain Vladimir Kovacevic who had already taken over the position of battalion commander. And he told me that when I arrived. So probably after Devlic was wounded, Captain Kovacevic probably took over his position immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Until Captain Devlic was wounded, who was the former battalion commander, did Captain Kovacevic have any position in that battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. He was the deputy battalion commander by establishment. He was there, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when you returned in mid-November and reported to Captain Kovacevic, the new battalion commander, did he give you any assignment? Did he send you anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: He offered me the possibility of choosing the duties I would like to take in the battalion, with the exception of his position, of course. And I told him that I wanted nothing more than to take up my former duties; that is, to return to my company which was then positioned in the village of Cajkovici, the tower of Gradci, and the tower of Strincjera.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher show the witness Exhibit P10, please, Prosecution Exhibit P10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, can you please look at the map and show us the deployment of your company when you returned to it in mid-November.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: My company was deployed along the Dubrovacka Rijeka and in Cajkovici village. It was also in the tower of Gradci and the tower of Strincjera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where the other companies from your battalion were at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please show us their positions.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: When I returned to my unit, together with the commander I made the rounds of the entire battalion in order to familiarise myself with the positions of the companies in the battalion. The village of Bosanka --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can the map be moved a little.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The village of Bosanka, Captain Stojanovic with the 1st Company was there. The village of Zarkovica, the anti-armour company with Captain Nesic. And here, I can't see any further. But there was the command in Gornji Brgat village at the railway station of Uskoplje. There was the mortar company. And in the Vlastica sector, there was, as you could see in the old map, the one that I can see on the desk next to me, if you gave me that map I could show it to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Lemal. Can you please repeat where the command of the 3rd Battalion was, and can you please go slowly and tell us where all the companies were.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Can you please give me a different map.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be given map P132.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, please tell me where the command of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade was.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Here, in the Gornji Brgat village above the road leading to Bosanka village at the far end of Gornji Brgat village towards Bosanka village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, you have already showed us your company in Strincjera.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Here, we have Cajkovici, the tower of Gradci, and the tower of Strincjera with my company there. The village of Bosanka, the 1st Company belonging to Captain Stojanovic. Zarkovica, Captain Jovica Nesic, the anti-armour division. Uskoplje, the railway station, the mortar company. It's captain was Zlatan Jeremic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please show us all those places on the map if you can.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is Uskoplje, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. And the rear company remained in Ivanica. It was a part of our battalion. In the Vlastica sector, there were ZIZ cannons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In other words, this is -- this was the deployment of your battalion when you rejoined it in mid-November 1991 upon your return from the medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me how long did your unit stay in these positions, up to what time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: We stayed in those positions -- I couldn't say precisely, but it was after the 6th of December when we received an order to withdraw from those positions back to the holiday settlement. I couldn't give you the exact date, but it was already in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we then say with certainty that you were in those same positions at the beginning of 1992 without any changes?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were abreast of the combat operations of your unit during the month of November, were there any incentives for unit members with regard to those combat operations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. There were incentives following those combat operations. On my return to the unit in consultation with Momcilo Bodiroga, Lieutenant Milan Stojanovic, and Lieutenant Sreten Nikolic who had been there, I personally proposed some of the soldiers and officers from my company for citations and commendations.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have the usher's assistance in giving the witness the next document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you your recommendations for incentives [as interpreted] and commendations. Did you send them to the commander of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did it in writing with the explanation for every individual who was proposed for an award because that was the common practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is my duty to explain in view of the volume of the document and the time that we received this document. The Defence has had the opportunity to translate only the title page and the second part of the document which is in handwriting. And this is going to be clarified with this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, can you please look at the first page of this document. Can you please tell us whose document it is.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: This document was produced by the command of the 9th Military Naval Sector and it was sent to the units on the 26th of November, 1991 at 1800 hours from the forward command post in Kupari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who signed it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: It was the Chief of Staff of the military naval sector, Milan Zec, the frigate captain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see who the addressee on the document is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: It was sent to the 3rd Infantry Brigade and the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, no, no. It says here: "Here enclosed please find the recommendations for simulation measures for the 3rd Light Infantry Brigade." And who is the addressee? Who was this document sent to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: To the command of the military naval sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Assistant commander for moral guidance, Zarkovic, Mihajlo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the next page, or behind that page there is also a recommendation for the light infantry brigade. This document is in B/C/S only. We haven't had it translated. Can you please look at the second part of the document which is in handwriting. Can you please tell us whose document is this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: This is a document which originates from the 3rd Battalion, from our battalion. And this is the handwriting of the commander, Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You recognise his handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: He signed it himself, Vladimir Kovacevic. And here, there are my soldiers on the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The list is rather long. Are there members of your unit that had been recommended by yourself for incentive measures?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, are there any names on the first page, and can you give us the number under which you find those names, if there are any?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Under 4, a soldier Arpad Sabo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is under II, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, it is. He is recommended for a 10-day leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he from your company, Arpad Sabo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the second page, are there any soldiers from your company?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: There must be, but these are mostly soldiers whose names I may have forgotten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the third page, can you remember any of the names?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. Under 8, Roman I, Captain First Class Milan Gasic, my deputy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is Roman VIII under 1? You recommended him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. He was captain, and he was recommended for promotion into the rank of the captain first class.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see any other names?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I don't recognise any here. Yes. Under VII. VII, under 5. Lieutenant Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's on page 3?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, it is on page 3. Second Lieutenant Nikolic is being promoted into the rank of lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on page 4, is there a name that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, there is. Soldier under X, under number 4, soldier Marko Komarica, awarded a medal for courage. X, under number 9, Milan Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they from your company?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, they are. And then under number XI, Todor Kecovic, posthumously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this document into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution objects again on the same basis that this is again a document which has connection to the 9th VPS and was not put to Admiral Jokic when he was being cross-examined. On that basis, the Prosecution objects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D100.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document is headed "Command of the 3rd Motorised Brigade." Should it be battalion, Mr. Rodic, in the translation in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In B/C/S version, it says, "Command of the 3rd MTB," which stands for the 3rd Motorised Battalion. In the English translation, it says, "Command of the motorised brigade." So there is a mistake in the translation. We're talking about the 3rd Battalion here. I apologise for the error in translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, these incentives or awards which were proposed for those individuals, were they in respect of the previous combat operations, in respect of the previous period during which these individuals did something good?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. It was in respect of the period starting with the 23rd October until mid-November when Gornji Brgat, Zarkovica, Bosanka and those parts of the plateau were taken up. Those areas were taken up while I was absent from the unit. And during that period, these individuals were -- deserved those awards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the company commanders or other officers receive recommendation for promotion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: No, none of the company commanders. But the battalion commander, Captain Kovacevic, was recommended for promotion by the command of the 472nd Brigade from Trebinje. And that's when he was promoted into captain first class, upon the recommendation of that command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the reason for this recommendation for promotion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. In the explanation, it said that he was recommended for promotion for his successful command and leadership of his units during the taking up of the aforementioned areas, Gornji Brgat, Zarkovica, Bosanka, during those combat operations, there were no casualties. And this was considered a successful combat operation. That is why he was recommended for promotion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, your positions at Strincjera, that is to say, the positions of your units, did you have a view of the situation from up there? I'm speaking in visual terms now. Could you see the other side, the enemy side, their military positions, their activities?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: From Strincjera, because this is trig point 412, I had a rather good view of Dubrovnik, from the Medarevo hospital towards the right, towards Babin Kuk, the Port of Gruz. The Srdj repeater did not allow me to see the entire town. It stood in between.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please put the map on the ELMO once again. Could it please be enlarged a bit so that we can see the left-hand side as well, Babin Kuk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate to us now from Strincjera how far could you see and what was it that you could keep under your control as far as the town of Dubrovnik is concerned?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: From the town -- from the tower of Strincjera, I could not see everything because of Srdj there. But then I could see Boninovo, the bay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the map please be lifted a bit so we could see its entirety. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Towards Babin Kuk, the Port of Gruz, and this entire area, from here. I could see all of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on map P10, at this moment, the witness is showing the view that he had from Strincjera and which parts of the town of Dubrovnik he could see from the positions of his company. It is Lapad, Babin Kuk, and the border --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the border towards the Old Town to the east? What was the last thing you could see?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: It is the bay, here, in the area of Boninovo where it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Boninovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, Boninovo. I couldn't see any further than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me in terms of the area that you indicated whether you noticed any firing positions of the enemy within that area? Were there any, and if so, where were they?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: There were stationery and mobile ones. When I say mobile ones firing points, I am referring to the so-called Charlie. I am referring to various improvised vehicles on which various types of weapons were mounted. It is the so-called Croatian armoured carrier which was added on to a truck, and then there was the Charlie vehicle with the mortars. And that's the one we could see most often along this road. From here, this is where the Libertas Hotel was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: And now this road that goes from here all the way up to Babin Kuk, that's where it moved most often. Then here in Lapad, if necessary, it's this street called Iva Vojnovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the record reflect that the witness is indicating the road from the Libertas Hotel, the street called Put Iva Vojnovica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To Lenin's Bulevar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So going from the stadium to Lenin Bulevar. So can we just reiterate whether this road that you showed now, does this have to do with where this vehicle moved along?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Charlie most often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain what "Charlie" was.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: This is a light transportation vehicle. It is a TAM light truck, up to two and a half tonnes. And a mortar was mounted on it of different calibres. And from there, it was possible to shoot successfully. Usually on roads -- I mean, people would come out with sighting devices. The elements would be established vis-a-vis the desired targets and then an X would be put there. And then when the vehicle comes to that particular point, it is possible to open fire very successfully and very quickly, and to move further on from that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever observe such action?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I did observe such action from the area of the stadium. I was not the target, but the adjacent unit at Osojnik was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was firing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: It was the Croatian side from the area of the stadium. They were firing from such a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Charlie vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, this Charlie vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you mentioned stationary firing positions. Where did you notice them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Stationary firing points were observed in the Lapad area. It cannot be seen here, but there were some tennis grounds here. And there was a small thicket or a park perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what are you showing here? Velika Petka, where it says Velika Petka?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, below trig point 197. The road itself is called Ispod Petka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the previous position you mentioned? You mentioned Lapad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. It says Put Ispod Petka Lapad. That is what is written here, and it is in that area that mortars were observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you notice any such thing in other parts of town?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Near the Libertas Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you have on the map here in addition to the text that you are showing? Can we indicate it for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The very corner where it says Kotorska Ulica. By the letter K, there is a numeral, 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it that you noticed there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I cannot say with any degree of precision whether it was a mortar or a cannon. But it certainly was an artillery piece that was firing from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you have a view of the Port of Gruz and Babin Kuk?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I had a view of Babin Kuk. I had a view of part of the Port of Gruz, although we controlled it by way of reconnaissance, moving to this other area from where one could observe it. So as far as Gruz is concerned, we cannot see this because this is black and white. But then on the other map, we can see this, the house right next door to the church, in the yard, there is a concrete garage underneath some vines. And every day at 2.00 exactly, they gathered there for lunch. We saw that. We observed that. But we did not do anything. But this is where they did collect. And they gathered there and probably they came down from Srdj to there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any positions that you could see in Rijeka Dubrovacka, in that area?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Well, in principle, Rijeka Dubrovacka could not be seen from this position up here, from Strincjera, or from Gradci, and I did keep under control Rijeka Dubrovacka and Sustjepan and the Cajkovici Stara Pruga [phoen] area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who held this side, Sustjepan? Were your units on that side?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: No, no. Sustjepan was held by Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the map please be moved a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They held Sustjepan. The Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any direct contact with Croatian units in Sustjepan because of the proximity?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Well, there were provocations by their forces, especially from Sustjepan. It was very hard for me to control the area because there is a slope going down towards the coastline, and it's rather inaccessible as can be seen from the configuration of the terrain. Often there were provocations from the direction of Sustjepan because, in fact, they were up to here. These underground tanks for fuel. This is practically up to where their control went, in this area above the railroad. So there were provocations. Two soldiers were wounded at Gradci. They were wounded in the legs or feet by fire coming from Sustjepan. They could mostly open fire towards Gradci because they did not have a good view of Strincjera either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When you refer to provocations, I'm interested in this period, the middle of November when you returned to the unit and, say, up to the 6th of December, 1991. How could you describe this for us? My question has to do with intensity, the intensity of these provocations.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Due to the configuration of the terrain, I could not deploy the units in the kind of combat order that is required from a tactical point of view. The platoon that was in Cajkovici, I had to supply around the surrounding road via Gornji Brgat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher for his assistance. Could he move the map or can it be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has to be a different map because it is not on this map anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown map P132, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we please have this particular position zoomed in. Thank you. Mr. Lemal, can you point this out now.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Here, from Cajkovici itself, I had to supply the unit all the way around Rijeka Dubrovacka, all the way up to Gornji Brgat, and then through the village of Bosanka, through this bay to Strincjera and Gradci. There is a part of the road here below Gradci, Gradci, to Strincjera which was not covered in bush, but there was an open road. This is where the Croatian Army targeted me the most, from Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Srdj, and this uncovered part.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Srdj is here, and the uncovered part is here. Between Strincjera and Gradci. There is a road here which led to Strincjera itself, and then from Strincjera to Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that part of the road, is that where the provocations took place?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Well, here, it was not possible to prepare food or to have any water supplies, so I had to supply the units every day from the area of the village of Bosanka. These trucks for bringing food and water were targeted most often from Strincjera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I made a mistake. From Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please say where the trucks were targeted from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: From the side where the Srdj repeater is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Trucks through which you supplied your company were targeted. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. Breakfast, lunch, dinner. Most often we would bring in lunch, and dinner and breakfast, too. So we usually had this transportation once a day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. So these were provocations coming from Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Sustjepan also.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please be asked not to speak at the same time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had provocations from Strincjera. But I responded with fire, and then it stopped, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, did you lodge any protests in relation to these provocations and this fire against your units?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: As for my positions up there at Strincjera, I really don't know what rank he held, but this man's name is Sofronija. I'm an infantry man, and these are navy men. And who else came? Was this a representative of the European Community. His name was Ramirez; he was a Spaniard. He wore white. And they came when those two soldiers of mine were wounded at Gradci. And that's when I cautioned against this, when I said what kind of things they did, they opened fire, et cetera, and of course I reported all of this to my commander as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, the man named Sofronija wearing a navy uniform, from which command did he come?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: He came from the command in Kupari, from the forward command post in Kupari. That is the VPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 9th Military Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he come to see you only once?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: No, he came frequently. And not just him. Others, too, would come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as for this Spaniard, Ramirez, from the observer mission, did he come to your position only once?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: No, he also came several times. He also came to Gradci, to Strincjera, and to Cajkovici. In fact, in Cajkovici, he attended certain negotiations that we had with the Croatian side to take over the dead from the Strincjera tower. That is, their soldiers who had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you have any memories linked to those contacts?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. I have some photographs from that event as a memento showing Sofronija, myself, and the Spaniard, Ramirez. Those photographs are at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be willing to show us those photographs and to provide the Court with that particular photograph showing Sofronija, Ramirez and yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, while you were at those positions held by your company - and again, we're talking about the period mid-November to the 6th of December, 1991 - were you visited by any other senior officer from the naval sector?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. Others would come, too, battleship captain Milan Zec.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: He was the Chief of Staff in the VPS. Then another visitor was Zarkovic. He was in charge of moral guidance, deputy commander for moral guidance. Then Kozaric, who was head of operations in the VPS. Then Gavro Kovacevic, a colonel, who was in charge of us, the infantry. He was assistant commander for the infantry. And Sofronija. I don't know exactly what his position was, but he would always come accompanied by foreigners coming either from the European Community or a delegation that would come with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell me, please, during these visits by the senior officers from the 9th Naval Sector and its command and their tours, did you have any discussions with them? Did they ask you anything?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: We did have talks with them. Mostly the story referred to the position of the units, whether the men were satisfied in view of the very poor conditions for life and accommodations. Then we would draw their attention to the provocations coming from Srdj when we were supplying my unit. And initially, there was fire on Strincjera as well until we returned the fire. But the provocations continued in the area of the village of Bosanka. So we mainly complained to them about these provocations coming from Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you have already explained in detail the positions of the companies of the 3rd Battalion, my question is, was there a logistics battalion in the -- a logistics platoon in the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, there was. It was part of the 3rd Battalion. And it was accommodated at Ivanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps I've gone a bit longer with the time for the break. So I don't know whether this would be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is a convenient moment. Could I point out that the time spent with this witness so far has been quite lengthy. And it's going to be difficult to finish him today, which I think ought to be done. So would you be very mindful of time when we resume. I propose that we break until 2.00 to enable a quick bite of food to be had. And we'll continue then at 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I move on, Mr. Lemal, can you please look at the map that you have in front of you and the positions of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade. Can you please look at the place where it says "Strincjera" and the red sign showing that position. What number can you read here?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The number is for the 3rd Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What company were you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I was the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a wrong entry?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, it is wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on. Within the battalion, did you have regular briefings?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. We had regular briefings with the battalion commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's speed up a little. And can you tell me where the briefings were.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Those were most often in his command post, and sometimes the commander would make rounds of all of us after the meetings to convey the messages from the meetings. And sometimes it was in Ivanica with the commander of the mortar company because he had electricity there. If those briefings were in the evenings, it was most often that they took place there because there was light.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me, please, do you know if your commander, Kovacevic, attended those briefings; and if he did, where did these briefings take place?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. He did go for briefings to Kupari, to the forward command post of the military naval sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Kupari to the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, a couple of times. Because my colleague from school provided security there as a member of the military police company. I would go there to meet with him. I would take a ride together with Kovacevic, but just to see my colleague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you participate in the attack on Srdj on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how did it happen that you participated in this attack?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: On the 5th of December, in the evening I was called from the command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you. When you say "the command post," can you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I got a call from Captain Kovacevic who was in Gornji Brgat. I'm referring to that command post. I received an order to report to the command post of Captain Jeremic in Ivanica. And we were to wait there for the arrival of our commander from a briefing. This order was conveyed by telephone. We were to wait for him there for our briefing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that moment - I apologise - where was the battalion commander at that moment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: He was at a briefing in Kupari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him before you started your meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him before we started our meeting. He arrived after us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which road did he take to get there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Since at that moment I was in Cajkovici, I took my car from Cajkovici, and at the crossroads in Gornji Brgat, I took a road to the left towards Ivanica, and I saw a vehicle driving after me from the direction of Dubac. As I pull over at Jeremic's command post, the car pulled over after me and Kovacevic was in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which direction are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: It is Kupari-Dubac-Gornji Brgat-Ivanica. That's the direction from which he came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly what was said during that briefing when the commander came?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The commander told us that the attack on repeater station on Srdj had been approved by the superior command. And together with him, we started discussing the way the mission would be accomplished and how the troops would be moved and from where in order to attack Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which is the superior command?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I suppose that since he had come from Kupari, that it would be the VPS.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness is being asked to speculate. In fact, his response, "I suppose" indicates that he is in fact speculating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think his evidence will go as far as that he came from Kupari. The rest appears to be speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour, although even during the first session I had questions relative to that command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the witness who or what was the superior command of the 3rd Battalion whose member you were.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The VPS, the military naval sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that briefing, were you assigned specific duties or missions for your units in respect of the attack on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. Every unit and every commander received a specific task and assignment as to what they're supposed to do and at what time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any support planned for the attack on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Within the assignment of missions, the battalion commander informed us that during the attack we would have support from the units stationed in the Cilipi sector and that we would also be supported by Lieutenant Colonel Jovanovic's unit from Mount Ostojnik [phoen]. In addition to our support units on the strength of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are the units from your battalion that were supposed to give you support?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: It was the mortar company, 120-millimetre mortar company, and ZIZ cannons on Vlastica mountain as I've already said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the artillery from Cilipi as your support?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of artillery are we talking about? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: It was long-range artillery, 130-millimetre cannons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after the end of this briefing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: After the end of this briefing, I went to Strincjera tower. I gathered my squad commanders. I informed them about the assignment that we had received from the battalion commander. One of my tasks was to select volunteers from my company and establish an assault group which would carry out an attack from Strincjera on the Srdj repetition station -- repeater station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people from your company were supposed to take place in that attack, in that assault group?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: During the briefing with the commander, I suggested that the group should not consist of more than 20 to 25 people, bearing in mind the configuration of the terrain. The commander accepted my proposal and that's why I selected 20 people from my company. I was also with a group together with my escort and the tank group. So altogether, there were 26 of us on that axis including the tank crew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your return from the briefing, did anybody else come to the positions of your company on Strincjera tower?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: It was Milan Zec, the warship captain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his position?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: He was the Chief of Staff in the VPS in Admiral Jokic's staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do at your company's positions? Why did he come?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I had asked for support for my mission. And since our target was a very inaccessible, fortified position, I asked for some equipment, for some flak jackets, for some plastic explosive, and a certain number of grenades for temporary destruction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you ask this support from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I asked this from my battalion commander during the briefing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive the equipment that you had requested?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. I received them between 2230 hours and midnight. I received all that from Captain Zec who had brought that to the Strincjera fortress.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what Captain Zec brought to you to Strincjera?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: He brought ten flak jackets. I don't know exactly how many kilos of explosives. And he also brought the AG and AGF grenades which are used for the temporary destruction of troops. He brought four or five pieces of those grenades. He did not bring as many as I requested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he talk to you? Did he say anything to you? I'm referring to Captain Zec.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. He always referred to me as "kiddo," and he asked me, "kiddo, are you prepared to carry out your mission? Did you select your men? Do you have any problems?" I told him I didn't have any. And then he went to have a quick word with the volunteers that had been selected from my unit, so he talked to them as well. He explained the importance of the facility that was being attacked. He said it would be good that if the mission could be accomplished and if the whole plateau could be taken up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually distribute this equipment that you received to the volunteers who were supposed to take part in this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any comments related to the distributed equipment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: There were. Since warship Captain Zec is a shortish man, and there was a volunteer who was also rather short, when he put on a flak jacket it went all the way down to his knees. So he was practically completely protected. And then Captain Zec laughed at that, and we commented upon it at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, the 6th of December, 1991, when did you set out? What time was agreed for starting the attack? Was there any synchronisation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: There was synchronisation. The agreement was that I and Lieutenant Pesic - I from Strincjera and Pesic from the village of Bosanka - at 5.00 in the morning while it was still dark, we should take our units out and get them as close as possible to the repeater at Srdj while it was still dark, which is what I did. And that's what he most probably did, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What unit did this Officer Pesic come from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The 1st Company, Captain Stojanovic's company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, did you have any attack preparations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: We did prepare the attack. Around 6.00 in the morning, around 6.00 in the morning, our ZIZ cannons opened fire at the lower area of fortification at Srdj where firing points were noticed. Machine-guns, snipers that were dug in, and it would be difficult to overcome them otherwise, and mortar fire started at the Srdj repeater itself which was a sign for me to continue my advance with the infantry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This fire preparation of the attack, did it go on all the time or were there intermissions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Well, there were intermissions because these weapons have a certain safety limit for their own forces, too; that is the so-called wider angle and narrow angle. When I came 400 to 600 metres away from the repeater itself, I fired a signal rocket which was the -- a signal to stop our artillery fire for the sake of our own forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, as you -- I withdraw this question. So, fire preparation was stopped at the moment when you got closer to the Srdj repeater.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you proceed from there, you with your troops?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: At that moment, on this main part of the road linking Strincjera and Srdj, this assault group was divided into two subgroups. One group went to the right consisting of ten men, and it was led by Lieutenant Nikolic. To the left of the road, there was another group of ten soldiers led by Momcilo Bodiroga. I together with my escort went along the road, and there was this tank that was supporting our group that went along the road as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to the tank as you advanced?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: From that moment on, since the artillery stopped firing at the repeater itself, they most probably took their positions. And in this further advance, this tank was hit, the tank that was escorting our group. It was hit through the external fuel tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return the tank, then?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: For the sake of safety and security, and since the tank crew had not been hurt, I issued an order for the tank to go back 500 or 600 metres to the back slope of that hill so that they could not fire at it any longer and that it could go on supporting us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know Marko Komarica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He was a soldier of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dakovic Svetislav?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mesaros?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these people who took part in that action?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, these groups of yours, that is to say, your group and the one you mentioned, Pesic's, from the direction of Bosanka, did they meet up at some point at Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. This happened as we entered the fort itself, through the gate. Or rather, these facilities that are up there. As we entered them, the left wing group that was led by Bodiroga and where Dakovic was and where Komarica was, met up with the left flank, that is to say, the right-hand group let by Lieutenant Pesic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these groups reach the plateau of Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were enemy soldiers then, those who were at the positions of fort Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: They retreated from these positions that were around the repeater itself and that were visible. They went into the underground premises that are underneath the repeater. Two or three storeys below the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any fire opened on the JNA assault groups that were advancing on the Srdj plateau?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: At that moment when we practically took the repeater, on the surface, on the ground there weren't any Croatian soldiers. At that moment, strong artillery, or rather mortar fire started on the Srdj plateau, and this fire was opened by the Croatian forces. There are rocky surfaces and concrete surfaces there, so for quite a while, we were subjected to strong fire by the Croat forces on that plateau.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, were there any consequences due to that fire?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: There were consequences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the consequences?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: In my assault group, Miroslav Tasovac got killed, Bozo Divljan got killed, Selajdin got killed. Three of my men were killed. Selajdin was an active-duty soldier. In Pesic's group, he himself as wounded . Soldier Mesaros got killed, and we had quite a few wounded and injured men as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This fire from Dubrovnik that was opened at you while you were at the Srdj plateau, how long did it last?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There has been no evidence in the English language as to the source of the fire, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I'll try to resolve that by rephrasing my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said while you were at the Srdj plateau, that mortars were firing at you. And I asked you, and you told me that you had sustained losses by that -- due to that fire. Do you know who it was that was firing at you and from where?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The fire came from the Croat side, from the area -- from the area of Lapad. Mortar fire was opened at the repeater Srdj itself. That is where we were at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to us what kind of fire was opened at you and how long it all lasted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: At the very outset, it was to a lesser degree probably until they adjusted their sighting equipment so as to target the repeater itself. Later on, it was synchronised fire, non-stop, constant fire, at the repeater.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, during the attack, did you have some kind of radio communication with the commander?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I did have radio communication with the commander. I was at the receiving end all the time. We were coordinating everything whenever necessary. There was very little need to communicate with me, but we could hear communication with the other leaders of groups who took part in the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive orders to retreat at any point?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who issued that order to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The commander of the battalion, Captain Kovacevic, issued an order for us to retreat to our starting positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the first time that this order to retreat was issued, when you heard it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Well, I contacted him in that period when we observed where we were being fired from. And since this was outside the range of my own equipment, I asked him to intervene so that that firing point at Lapad could be neutralised because we were suffering heavy gunfire, and we also started incurring losses. After a while, he issued an order to me to withdraw my men to the starting position and to bear in mind that gunfire as we were retreating to the starting positions. He issued me an order to retreat only once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It has been a long time. But do you happen to remember approximately what time this was? So you don't have to be very accurate. Do you remember approximately the time when you retreated?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: At any rate, it was in the afternoon. At any rate, it was in the afternoon. It was after midday because as we returned to Strincjera, it got dark very soon. So at any rate, it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your unit withdrew to its starting position at Strincjera?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Strincjera, was medical aid provided to anyone? What did you do with your dead and wounded?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: First of all, as far as the dead are concerned, with the assistance of the tank I managed to pull them out towards the Strincjera tower. Also, the wounded, whereas those who were only lightly wounded withdrew on their own. It took quite a while, this retreat. We were withdrawing in groups. And Dr. Vukas came with medical vehicles. He took over the dead and wounded and took them in the direction of Kupari so that the wounded could be taken care of. The dead were immediately transferred to the Trebinje hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, on the 6th of December 1991 when you returned to Strincjera, to your starting position, where were you until the end of that day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I was at the tower of Strincjera itself. I talked to all my men and told them to be cautious and alert during the night. I was there all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, did anybody come to see you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The commander of the battalion came, and I cannot say exactly but either Sofronija or Zarkovic came for sure. One of the two came for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sofronija is the officer who you mentioned earlier on.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, the one who came with the foreigners. And Zarkovic is the one from moral guidance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they ask you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: They asked me in general what the morale of the men was like, whether there was any dissatisfaction, how they received what had happened. That's what it boiled down to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any protest among your fighters?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, there was. Primarily because this artillery support was not carried out at the firing point which had directly caused the death of three of our comrades and others from the other company. So that is what was said to them directly when they came, but nobody knew the answer why there was not any support, especially the commander said that he did not know why artillery support was not granted in respect of that firing point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The previous day during the briefing with the commander, you were promised such support?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, we were. Because we knew that they were firing positions on Lokrum and on Babin Kuk which were out of the range of our equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 7th of December, the day after, where were you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: On the 7th of December, I was still with my unit. I was on Strincjera all the time up to midday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave Strincjera at any time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to make rounds of my unit that was in Cajkovici. I descended to the command post in Gornji Brgat. I pulled over, and I asked if the commander was there. Then they told me that the commander was not at the command post, and I only asked them to convey the message that I was in Cajkovici. And then I continued driving to Cajkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 8th of December, were you with your unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Around 10.00 I left my unit together with a group of men, and I went to Kravarevo [phoen], village of Baba Gacko [phoen] to attend the burial of Bozo Divljan. Another group went to Trebinje to attend another funeral, the funeral of Tasovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did somebody question you about the events, that is, the attack on Srdj on the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: No, nobody did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you write any reports and send it to anybody about that attack?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your regular briefings in the -- in your battalion's command, were you informed about the positions and the strength and the activities of the enemy side, of the other side?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, I was. During the briefings, the commander would inform us about the incidents and the activities of the enemy targeted at our neighbouring units. Company commanders Stojanovic and Nesic who were deployed on Zarkovica and in Bosanka voiced their protests with the commander against the fire opened from Stari Grad on their units that were located there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These provocations against their units, were they very frequent from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Captain Nesic who was on Mount Zarkovica complained about that very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any arms, any types of arms mentioned when there were discussions about the fire being opened from Stari Grad on Zarkovica and in Bosanka?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: During those briefings, he mentioned the anti-aircraft, 20-millimetre cannon. He also mentioned heavy machine-guns and a mortar in the sector of the entry into Stari Grad. I don't exactly remember the name of that place that he mentioned. He also mentioned the snipers that are active from the houses around those hotels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, since you were also a teacher in the school for reserve officers in Bileca, is a mortar an infantry weapon?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The 60, the 82-millimetre, and the 120-millimetre mortars are all infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can a mortar be used to open fire from a hard surface?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, it can with adequate preparation. It can be used to open fire from a hard surface. And this is very well explained in the rules for the use of mortar fire. The hard surface can be sacks with sand or a soft wood or any other hard surface that is prepared for the fire to be opened by a mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This type of training for opening mortar fire, was that something that you taught your students in Bileca?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the 6th of December during the following seven to ten days, did any high officer, a general or admiral, visit the positions of your company or your battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: No. I never saw a general or an admiral coming to the position of my units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any higher or superior command in the Dubrovnik and Herzegovina theatre of war in addition to the 9th Military Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The first time I learned of the existence of the 2nd Operations Group in Trebinje was when I addressed -- approached the command in Bileca for them to approve a vehicle that I would use to move my stuff. Then I was told that I should talk to the command of the 2nd Operations Group in Trebinje. That was in February 1992. I moved my family from Bileca in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only briefly, were you ever visited by the officers from the 9th VPS after the 6th of December? Did they come to the positions of the 3rd Battalion and your company?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, they did. All those officers whose names I've mentioned came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they control the situation? Did they inquire about the situation in the unit after the battle on Srdj on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, they did. That was very soon after the incident on the 6th of December. They still wanted to know if there was any dissatisfaction, what was the situation like, what we were going to do next. In any case, the 6th of December continued to be a topic of discussion in our unit for a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me if anybody was awarded or decorated as a result of what happened on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not sure about the time. I don't know when we're supposed to adjourn today. I have two very brief questions to put to the witness, and I would also like to show him two very short documents, and then I'll be able to complete my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. Can the witness be shown Exhibit D98.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Defence counsel, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, in this document, can you please look at the part where it says that the unit has been replenished and the plastic explosives are being mentioned, AG1 Zolja, and 7- and 9-millimetre bullets for the sniper. Can you please explain to us what re AGs and AFs.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Those are special grenades based on the chemicals for the momentaneous [as interpreted] destruction of troops without long-term consequences for the troops. Momentaneous, temporary. So it is a grenade similar used by the police during demonstrations. This is the type of grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have P24. Can this be put before the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, in this photo, do you recognise something? Does something look familiar to you in these photos?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The lower photo depicts the so-called HOD [phoen], the Croatian armoured vehicle which used a lorry as its base. I opened fire on it. I didn't hit it, though. It was in Rijeka Dubrovacka near the gas station. This is the first time I saw it before we took those positions. And later on, I saw it in the part of the Gruz harbour and Lapad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this completes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rodic. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Mahindaratne:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lemal. My name is Prashanthi Mahindaratne, and I will ask you some questions on behalf of the Prosecution. Mr. Lemal, you indicated in examination-in-chief that you attended the school centre of the infantry in Bileca and the school for unity and brotherhood. Can you perhaps just indicate what type of --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, our learned friend is not quoting the evidence properly. The witness didn't say that he attended that school in Bileca. He said that he was a teacher in that school. Could more attention be paid to the testimony of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I will rephrase perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me correct myself, Mr. Lemal. Your evidence was that you attended the school for brotherhood and unity in Belgrade, and the military academy for land forces, specifically the department of infantry division. Now, could you perhaps give us some idea as to what type of training did you receive at these institutions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: In the military grammar school, which is a secondary school that takes four years, I acquired general knowledge and general education. In addition to that, every year we would be sent for practical training. We would learn how to ski. We would have tactical training on Manjaca. And this was what was done during the secondary military school. At the military academy, however, since this was a school of higher education, we studied all of the existing weapons with the focus being put on those weapons that belonged to the branch of the military that we would later on belong to. After two years spent in Belgrade, I was transferred for specialisation in Sarajevo. That was also a military academy. I completed my education there. And I was able to have more practical education in the natural surroundings and in the situations very similar to the war situations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, you said that in mid-September you were temporarily transferred to the 472nd Motorised Brigade. And you reported to its command post which was located in Trebinje. Were you also aware at that time that the command post of the 2nd Operational Group was also located in Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: No. I've said that the first time I learned of the existence of command of the 2nd Operations Group was towards the end of February 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So right through the period mid-September until 1992, although you kept reporting to your brigade command in Trebinje, you did not know that there was another command post in Trebinje; namely, the command post of the 2nd Operational Group? That's your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: I never said I reported to the command of the brigade in Trebinje. I reported to my battalion command, Captain Kovacevic, who was at the command post in Gornji Brgat. Not for a single moment did I mention reporting to the command of the 472nd Brigade in Trebinje, save for the moment when I first reported to that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit Trebinje perhaps to visit the brigade, not in a formal sense of reporting. But did you visit Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The only time I was in Trebinje was the seven days that I spent in the hospital there, and on those occasions when I travelled home to Bileca. That is when I would pass through Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, you said that when you reported, because of your ethnic background, you were treated with some degree of suspicion or people were cautious when dealing with you. In that, did you mean that perhaps people did not inform you of what was going on around you because of this certain degree of cautiousness with which they treated you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: No. They didn't trust me to the extent one was supposed to trust their commander. And this lasted until the moment of our first combat activities when they saw my behaviour in combat. From that moment on, I did not have any problems with my people trusting me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not trusted because of your ethnic background or because you were transferred temporarily to the 472nd Motorised Brigade? Or what was the reason that you were not trusted by your units?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: The commander of that brigade, Nojko Marinovic, had abandoned that unit and defected to Croatia. And this was not the only case of Croatian officers or even Hungarian officers or actually of any of those who were not members of the Serbian or Montenegrin nations that abandoned their troops, and that's why people were cautious. And I did not think of this situation as being tragic. I knew that it would take time, but that finally everything would come in its own place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, just one question I should have asked you before: Where exactly is Sremska Mitrovica - I beg your pardon for the mispronunciation - the place you live at?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Sremska Mitrovica is in Vojvodina in the Republic of Serbia. It is 70 kilometres away from Belgrade in the direction of Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the witness be shown map P132.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lemal, with regard to this particular map, you indicated certain positions that the units of the 3rd Battalion had after November right through December. Now, could you please place your pointer on Strincjera where your unit was positioned.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That along with the positions to the north of Strincjera were taken by your units or were held by your units?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you indicated that the 1st Company held the position at Bosanka. Am I correct, or did I misunderstand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the name of the company commander of the 1st Company of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Captain Slavoljub Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The anti-tank weapons company which was commanded by Captain Nesic was positioned on Zarkovica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Anti-armour company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anti-armour.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Captain Jovica Nesic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please place your pointer on that location, Zarkovica, where his unit was deployed at. You have to push the map up a little upwards, Mr. Lemal.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which company was that? What was the number given to that company? Was it the 1st Company, the 2nd Company, the 3rd Company, or the 4th Company of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: No. Only infantry companies within a battalion have numbers. Companies like the mortar company, since it's the only one within the battalion, is only called the mortar company and the calibre of the mortar. So 120-millimetre company. And the anti-armour company, since there's only one of them, is called that anti-armour company. However, since infantry companies come in a multitude, then they are called he 1st, 2nd, 3rd, et cetera. And, for example, the logistics platoon, there is only one of them, so then there is no need for a numeral.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the 3rd Battalion, in addition to the anti-armour company, there were three other infantry companies. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LEMAL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
